Clearing the custom variable should prevent the error from popping up again. Here is the guide:

## Solution 4: Disable WoW Lua Errors

### FAQ/How to enable and disable script errors ("Lua errors")

In order to troubleshoot potential issues, particularly when the addon isn't loading correctly, you'll need to post any error messages Lua will display in the game. These are disabled by default in the most current client versions.  
  
You can, however, enable them using this command:

```
/console scriptErrors 1
```

Once you're done reporting a problem, and no longer wish to see error messages, feel free to disable them with this command:

```
/console scriptErrors 0
```

**Important: There is no confirmation after typing these commands, and you'll need to reload your interface or restart/relog to see the relevant error messages if Rarity failed to load.**

A LUA error in World of Warcraft means that one or more of your installed addons contains a script fault — a piece of code that crashed or behaved unexpectedly during gameplay. This is one of the most common issues WoW players face, especially after a major game patch when addons haven't yet been updated to match the new game version. The good news is that LUA errors are almost always fixable without any technical expertise, and you rarely need to contact Blizzard support.

Ad

## Tools You'll Need

* Battle.net Desktop App
* Addon manager (CurseForge, Overwolf, or WoW AddOn Manager)
* File Explorer (Windows) or Finder (Mac)
* Screenshot tool (optional, to capture error details)

## How to Fix Error Code LUA error

1. ### Read the Error Message Carefully
2.
### Disable the Offending Addon
3. ### Disable ALL Addons to Isolate the Cause
4. ### Update the Problematic Addon
5. ### Delete and Reinstall the Addon
6. ### Clear the WoW Cache and WTF Folders
   
   Renaming or deleting the WTF folder will erase all saved addon configurations, keybindings, and UI layout settings. Consider renaming it to WTF\_backup instead of deleting it so you can restore it if needed.
7. ### Run the Blizzard Repair Tool
8. ### Check for Addon Conflicts

Ad

## When to Call a Professional

LUA errors are almost exclusively caused by third-party addons and are not Blizzard bugs. You should contact Blizzard Support only if LUA errors appear with ALL addons disabled and the Scan and Repair tool finds no issues — this could indicate a deeper game installation problem. You can also reach out to the individual addon author via CurseForge comments or their GitHub repository if the addon is outdated and causing repeated errors after patches.
## Frequently Asked Questions

Why did I suddenly start getting WoW LUA errors after a patch?

After Blizzard releases a game patch, the game's internal API (the code addons use to interact with the game) often changes. Addons written for the previous version may call functions that no longer exist or work differently, causing a LUA script error. This is extremely common on patch day and usually resolves itself within a day or two as addon authors release updates. Is a WoW LUA error dangerous or will it corrupt my game?

No, a LUA error will not corrupt your game or account. At worst, the addon causing the error will stop functioning properly for that session. Your characters, progress, and game installation are completely safe. LUA errors are contained to the addon scripting environment and cannot affect core game files. How do I stop WoW LUA error popups without fixing the addon?

You can suppress LUA error popups by typing '/console scriptErrors 0' in the in-game chat box.
This hides the error window but does not fix the underlying problem — the addon may still malfunction silently. To turn error reporting back on, type '/console scriptErrors 1'. Some addons like BugSack or Swatter also manage error reporting with more detail. Which addons most commonly cause LUA errors in WoW?

Any addon can trigger a LUA error if it's outdated, but the most common culprits tend to be complex UI overhaul addons (like ElvUI or Tukui), action bar replacements (like Bartender4 or Dominos), and weakaura scripts that reference outdated spell or aura IDs. Addons that haven't been updated in several months are the highest risk after a major patch. Can I fix a LUA error myself by editing the addon code?

Yes, if you're comfortable with basic scripting, LUA errors often include a line number and file path in the error message. You can open the addon's .lua file in a text editor like Notepad++ and attempt to comment out or correct the faulty line.
However, this is only recommended if you have some coding experience. For most players, waiting for the addon author to release an update is the easier and safer option.

The _World of Warcraft_ game client stores all of its configurations in console variables ( **CVars** ). These variables affect many aspects of the game such as the graphics, the sound system and the interface.

The value of a CVar can be queried with GetCVar .
The complete list of CVars is available from C\_Console.GetAllCommands .

## Contents

* 1 Setting CVars
  
    + 1\.1 SetCVar
    + 1\.2 Console
    + 1\.3 Config.wtf
* 2 CVar Scope
* 3 Resetting CVars
* 4 List of Console Variables
* 5 List of Console Commands

## Setting CVars

There are several ways of setting the console variables. The most commonly used CVars are tied to the Interface window settings.

### SetCVar

AddOns and scripts can set CVars by calling SetCVar .

```
/ run SetCVar ( "scriptErrors" , 1 )
```

Note

**Note:** Secure CVars 🛡️ cannot be set in combat and only with `SetCVar` instead of with `/console` .

### Console

With the `/console` slash command.

```
/console scriptErrors 1
```

The `/console enable` command or launching the game with the `WoW.exe -console` argument will allow you to open the Console window in-game by pressing the ````` or `~` key.

Console variables 01.png

### Config.wtf

The Config.

...

Use GetCVarDefault or the cvar\_default command to reset a CVar, for example:

```
/ run SetCVar ( "autoSelfCast" , GetCVarDefault ( "autoSelfCast" ))
```

```
/console cvar_default autoSelfCast
```

The [AdvancedInterfaceOptions](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/advancedinterfaceoptions) addon can show which cvars were changed from the default:

AdvancedInterfaceOptions cvar browser

To reset the whole user interface:

```
/console cvar_default
```

results.title: How to prevent LUA errors in WoW The War Within
excerpts:
The best way to do this is through the CurseForge application where you can download the [best addons](https://dotesports.com/wow/news/best-addons-for-wow-the-war-within) for _The War Within_ .

The first thing you should do is check if any of your addons **need updating** . If everything’s in order, you can also download two of the following addons:

* BugGrabber
* BugSack

Both addons work together to prevent LUA errors from appearing on your screen. Another useful tip is to disable all addons and then enable them once more. If that doesn’t work, keep scrolling down for other methods.

### Reset WoW Console Variables

A short man with a long beard and a glowing blue bird mount in wow the war within Another useful trick. Screenshot by Dot Esports

This method is a bit different but impactful, and it just might be the solution you’re looking for.
**Console Variables or Cvar** in _WoW_ are essentially game client stores that affect many aspects of **graphics, sound, and, above all else, the Interface** .

You can use this method while you’re playing _The War Within_ , and all you have to do is type in the chat following commands:

* console Cvar\_reset
* console cvar\_default

These commands reset and restore the _WoW_ Console Variable to its default settings. Once you type them, **restart the game** and check if LUA errors are fixed.

### Completely disable LUA errors

Brann Bronzebeard holding a pickaxe and a torch in WoW The War Within. Deal with them once and for all. Image via Blizzard Entertainment

This effective method allows you to disable all LUA errors in _The War Within_ , but it should also be your last resort. All you have to do is type in chat the following scripts:

* /console scriptErrors 0 (disable LUA errors)
* /console scriptErrors 1 (enable LUA errors)
